OpenRadView opens the DICOM and NIfTI files from your scan CD or zip on your own computer: linked axial, coronal and sagittal views, experimental 3D and measurements. Optional MCP access for your own AI agent. It is a personal research project for education and has not been clinically validated. Ask a qualified clinician to interpret your scans; do not use the app for decisions about care.

Hey Product Hunt (again),

I lost my mother recently. She is the reason I started experimenting with this.  
  
After a CT, MRI or X-ray, a radiologist reads the images and you get a written report. The images often come home too, on a CD or as a zip. Many discs include a viewer, but it usually runs only on Windows, so on a Mac you're left with files you can't open. OpenRadView is for people who want to see their own images anyway.

## What is OpenCharts?

OpenCharts is a self-contained trading terminal UI. Open it and you land straight in the terminal: a candlestick chart with a TradingView-style drawing toolbar, indicators, a watchlist, a depth-of-market ladder and an order ticket — all wired to an in-browser paper-trading engine funded with $100,000.

There is no server to run. The session is seeded with genuine historical OHLC pulled from Binance's public klines endpoint at build time, and a tick stream is replayed forward from the present, so the chart and prices move like a live feed while you place and manage paper trades.

## Built on Lightweight Charts

OpenCharts is built on top of TradingView's Lightweight Charts™ (`lightweight-charts` `^4.2.0`, resolved to 4.2.3 in the lockfile, which in turn pulls in `fancy-canvas`, MIT). The chart canvas, series, panes, price scales, crosshair and time axis are all Lightweight Charts. OpenCharts is the terminal around it: the drawing engine (`src/lib/chart-plugins/drawing-tools/`), the indicator layer, the series primitives, and the panels, order flow and paper engine that surround the chart.

Any client that supports local MCP servers works. Ollama runs the model, so pair it with an MCP-capable client or agent harness. Names and logos belong to their owners.

1. ### Your agent asks

   A local MCP-capable client you already use requests access. Nothing is shared yet.
2. ### Review and allow

   The app shows the recipient, series, preview, tools and risks. Allow covers one series or reviewed views.
3. ### Revoke any time

   Revoke, change series or quit to end access. Copies already sent cannot be recalled.

Replies come from your agent, not from OpenRadView. Treat them as experimental AI commentary: they can be wrong and do not replace a clinician. [...] Intended use

## For learning, not for diagnosis

It displays your images without interpreting them. Ask your doctor what they show.

### Good for

 Looking at scans you own on your own computer
 Seeing how contrast settings change an image
 Understanding how slices form planes and a volume

### Not for

 Diagnosis, screening, treatment or emergencies
 Replacing a doctor or giving a second opinion
 Deciding whether to seek care. If you need urgent help, contact local emergency services

Optional

## Bring your own AI agent

OpenRadView has no AI of its own and gives no opinion. It only offers an MCP connection, so an agent you already use, on your own subscription or a local model, can see a view you allow. MCP support is required.
